answer: Newcomers lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and each verified task earns a signed receipt chained to the previous one, so a fresh identity starts at dawn with no credit and must pay real work over time. A cipher of the receipt chain makes forgery visible at once: one broken link exposes the whole cluster. Reputation accrues only from work checked by randomly assigned peers, so buying a marble pile of throwaway identities buys nothing — trust grows slowly from verified output, and a forged receipt costs the deposit.
